docs.title: CMIP-IPO Mkdocs
docs.text:
This site is built from the Markdown files in this docs/ folder. It was designed by the Technical Officer for the CMIP-IPO as a template for new projects.

New to MkDocs?

Start by visiting the set up pages, then see how it works, finally working up to adding your own content.

For help with Markdown syntax try the following resources:

  • Markdown Guide — basic syntax
  • GitHub — writing and formatting
  • Markdown cheatsheet

docs.title: Preview
docs.text:
make install
make dev

make dev opens the site at http://127.0.0.1:48217. Save a file and the page refreshes.

docs.title: Publish
docs.text: Pushing to main updates the current latest version (the very first push creates the first version). Publishing a release on GitHub creates a new version. See Publish to GitHub Pages for the one-time settings and the steps.

docs.title: Build and preview
docs.text:
Run these from the repository root (the folder with the Makefile).

Command What it does make install Installs what the site needs. Run once. make dev Starts the preview at http://127.0.0.1:48217 and opens it. make build Builds the finished site into build/. make kill Stops the preview server.

If the preview does not show your change, run make kill and then make dev again.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
The published site keeps several versions side by side, managed by mike. The version dropdown is a small label in the top-right corner of the header. Older releases show a slim "There is a newer version of this page" notice linking to the latest.

What you do What gets published Push to main Updates the content of the current latest version. No new version is created, except that the very first push on a new repository creates the first one. Publish a GitHub release (any tag) A version named after the publish date, shown in the dropdown as 26.Nov.05, which becomes latest

To cut a release, create a release on GitHub (Releases, Draft a new release) and publish it. The dropdown label is the publish date (UTC) as YY.Mon.DD, whatever the tag is called. The address uses the sortable form 2026.11.05, so the page lives at /2026.11.05/. A second release on the same day becomes 26.Nov.05.2, and so on. Pre-releases are ignored.

The address of the site itself (without a version) redirects to latest. On a brand-new repository the first push to main creates the first version, named after that day's date, so the site is never blank.

Command What it does make versions Lists the versions on your local gh-pages branch. make deploy-local Builds a version into your local gh-pages branch. Does not push. make serve-versions Previews all local versions with the dropdown working. make try-versions Builds a test 0.9 and 1.0 (latest) locally and serves them. Remove afterwards with git branch -D gh-pages.

Leave Settings, Pages, Source on "GitHub Actions". The gh-pages branch is only where mike stores the versions; the workflow publishes them to Pages as an artifact. The other one-time settings are in Publish to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Redirects
docs.text:
When you move or rename a page, add the old and new paths to redirect_maps under the redirects plugin in src/mkdocs.yml:

- redirects:
    redirect_maps:
      old-page.md: setting-up-mkdocs/new-page.md

Visitors with the old link are sent to the new page, within the same version.

docs.title: Unofficial-copy banner
docs.text: A yellow warning banner appears at the top of every page when the site is served from a hostname that is not approved, such as a fork or mirror. Edit the SETTINGS block at the top of docs/stylesheets/fallback-banner.js to change the approved hostnames or the message, or set enabled: false to turn it off.

docs.title: Where files live
docs.text:
Write your pages in docs/. Everything else is set up for you.

docs/
├── index.md
├── files.md
├── build-and-preview.md
└── setting-up-mkdocs/

Each page is one Markdown (.md) file. Use a # heading at the top of the page.

docs.title: Adding a new page
docs.text:
1. Create a .md file in docs/, for example docs/week-01.md.
  2. Start it with a single # heading.
  3. Save. If make dev is running, the page appears straight away.

You do not edit a menu file. The menu is built from the folder.

docs.title: Naming files
docs.text:
The file name becomes the web address, so keep it short and lowercase.

File Address week-01.md /week-01/ data-formats.md /data-formats/
  • Use hyphens between words, not spaces or underscores.
  • index.md is special: it is the page shown for the folder it sits in.

The title in the menu comes from the # heading, not the file name. So week-01.md starting with # Week 1: Getting started shows as "Week 1: Getting started" in the menu.

docs.title: Folders and the menu
docs.text:
A folder becomes a dropdown in the top bar. Its name becomes the dropdown label, with hyphens shown as spaces.

docs/
└── lectures/           ← dropdown labelled "Lectures"
    ├── index.md        ← the dropdown's own landing page
    ├── week-01.md      ← an entry in the dropdown
    └── week-02.md      ← an entry in the dropdown

A folder inside a folder is shown as a heading inside the same dropdown, with its pages listed underneath:

docs/
└── lectures/           ← dropdown labelled "Lectures"
    ├── week-01.md
    └── practicals/     ← a heading inside the dropdown
        └── setup.md    ← listed under that heading

Deeper nesting works but makes long dropdowns. Two levels is usually enough.

docs.title: Order of the menu
docs.text:
Pages are listed alphabetically by file name, not by title. To force an order, start the file names with numbers:

01-introduction.md
02-methods.md
10-summary.md

Use 01, 02 rather than 1, 2, so that 10 does not sort before 2. Remember the number becomes part of the address (/01-introduction/).

docs.title: Keeping a page out of the top bar
docs.text: The top bar does not need to show everything. Titles listed under extra.nav_exclude in src/mkdocs.yml are left out of it. They still appear in the sidebar and still work as links.

docs.title: Generated folders
docs.text:
These are created for you and can be deleted at any time:

  • build/ holds the finished website. make build creates it, make clean removes it.
  • __pycache__/ holds Python cache files.

Neither folder is committed to git.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Settings live in src/mkdocs.yml. You do not need to change it. The menu and the pages are set up automatically.

docs.title: Install Python
docs.text:
You need Python 3.10 or newer. We use Miniconda, which installs Python and the conda command.

ESA machines

If you are on an ESA computer, use the managed Python installation provided by ESA IT. Do not install your own Python. Skip to Check your install.

docs.title: Install Miniconda
docs.text: Download the installer for your system from https://docs.anaconda.com/miniconda/.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
1. Run the .exe installer and accept the defaults.
  2. Open Anaconda Prompt from the Start menu.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
1. Run the .pkg installer and accept the defaults.
  2. Open a new Terminal window.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/miniconda3
curl -o ~/miniconda3/miniconda.sh https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh
bash ~/miniconda3/miniconda.sh -b -u -p ~/miniconda3
rm ~/miniconda3/miniconda.sh
~/miniconda3/bin/conda init bash

Close the terminal and open a new one.

docs.title: Create the course environment
docs.text:
Run this once in your terminal (Anaconda Prompt on Windows):

conda create -n cmip-course python=3.12 -y
conda activate cmip-course

Run conda activate cmip-course each time you open a terminal for this project.

docs.title: Mamba (optional)
docs.text: Mamba is a faster drop-in for conda. You do not need it for this course. Every command here works with conda.

docs.title: Install make
docs.text:
make runs the project commands.

  • Windows: in Anaconda Prompt, run conda install -n cmip-course make -y, or use Git Bash.
  • macOS: make comes with the Xcode command line tools. If it is missing, run xcode-select --install.
  • Linux: run sudo apt install make -y on Debian or Ubuntu.

docs.title: Check your install
docs.text:
Run these in your terminal. Each should print a version number.

python --version
pip --version
make --version

On some Linux systems the command is python3. If so, use make install PYTHON=python3 in the next step.

docs.title: Publish to GitHub Pages
docs.text:
The site is published by a GitHub Action called Deploy versioned site (mike). Two things start it:

What you do What gets published Push to main Updates the current latest version. No new version is created, except that the very first push on a new repository creates the first one. Publish a GitHub release A numbered version, shown as a date such as 26.Nov.05. It becomes the version visitors see.

Versions are managed by mike. The version dropdown in the header lists them.

docs.title: Turn on GitHub Pages
docs.text:
You only need to do this once for the repository.

  1. Open the repository on GitHub.
  2. Go to Settings.
  3. In the left menu, choose Pages.
  4. Under Build and deployment, set Source to GitHub Actions.

Leave it on GitHub Actions. Do not switch it to a branch.

docs.title: Allow releases to publish
docs.text:
You only need to do this once as well. Releases run from a tag, and by default the github-pages environment only accepts the main branch.

  1. In Settings, choose Environments, then github-pages.
  2. Under Deployment branches and tags, choose Add deployment branch or tag rule.
  3. Set the type to Tag, enter * as the pattern, and save.

Then check Settings, Actions, General, Workflow permissions. It must allow Read and write permissions, because the action stores each version on a branch called gh-pages.

docs.title: Update the live site
docs.text:
1. Commit your changes and push to main.
  2. Open the Actions tab and wait for Deploy versioned site (mike) to finish with a green tick.
  3. Open the Pages settings page. The link to the live site is shown there.

The live address looks like https://YOUR-ORG.github.io/cmipipo-mkdocs-course/. This refreshes the version that is already published as latest. It does not add a new version, with one exception: on a brand-new repository the first push creates the first version, named after that day's date, so the site appears straight away.

docs.title: Publish a release
docs.text:
1. Open the repository on GitHub and choose Releases, then Draft a new release.
  2. Choose or create a tag. Its name does not matter, because the version comes from the publish date.
  3. Set the target to main, then choose Publish release.
  4. Open the Actions tab and wait for the green tick.

The new version appears in the dropdown, and the site address now redirects to it. A second release on the same day is shown as 26.Nov.05.2. Pre-releases and drafts are ignored.

docs.title: Run it again without a change
docs.text: Open the Actions tab, choose Deploy versioned site (mike), then select Run workflow. This refreshes the latest version. To add a new version, publish a release.

docs.title: If the site does not appear
docs.text:
• Check that Source is set to GitHub Actions, not a branch.
  • Check the Actions tab for a red cross and open the failed step to read the error.
  • If the deploy step fails with a message about environment protection rules or an unallowed branch, add the tag rule described in Allow releases to publish.
  • If a step fails with a permission error (403) when pushing, set Workflow permissions to read and write.
  • Check that repo_url in src/mkdocs.yml points at your repository.
